references.text: The command that nothing of the Passover lamb should remain until morning, parallel to the prohibition in Deuteronomy that the meat must not be left until morning.
The original command to remove leaven from houses for seven days during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The prohibition against having leaven in houses for seven days, with a warning of being cut off from the community.
Reiteration of the prohibition against leaven and that no leaven should be seen anywhere in the area for seven days.
Prohibition that the fat from the festival offering must not remain until morning.
The command that the meat of the Passover sacrifice must not be left until morning.
Paul uses leaven as a symbol of sin and urges the church to cleanse out the old leaven, referencing Christ as our Passover lamb.
